title: Randomness that unfolds
question: What is a random process, and what are its moving parts?
hook: Prices, phone calls and gas molecules all change by chance, and one idea describes them all.
idea: A stochastic process is a collection of random variables indexed by a set, often time, each taking values in a shared state space.

beats.prompt: A mathematician wants to model price changes on a stock exchange and also the number of phone calls in a period. Which pairing matches the classic uses?

choices.label: Poisson process for prices, Wiener process for call counts
choices.feedback: This reverses the classic uses; Bachelier used the Wiener process for prices.

choices.label: Wiener process for prices, Poisson process for call counts
Wiener process for both prices and call counts
choices.feedback: The two classic processes were each proposed for a different kind of phenomenon.

beats.explain: Bachelier used the Wiener process to model price changes on the Paris Bourse, while Erlang used the Poisson process to model phone calls in a period.

beats.prompt: Match each part of a stochastic process to what it is.
pairs: The set that labels the random variables, often read as time
The space of values each random variable takes
How much the process changes between two index values
A single outcome of the whole process
beats.explain: A process is a collection of random variables labelled by an index set, each taking values in the state space; one outcome is a realization.

beats.prompt: Sort each index set by the kind of time it gives.
items: An interval of the real line
beats.explain: A finite or countable index set gives discrete time, while an interval of the real line gives continuous time.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: A process has the integers as its index set and the real line as its state space.
Because the index set is the integers, it is a discrete-time process.
Because the state space is the real line, it is a real-valued process.
So it must be an integer-valued process, since it is discrete-time.
beats.explain: Integer-valued describes the state space, not the index set. With the real line as state space, the process is real-valued.
